pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Caelan? You're awake, aren't you?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Mother Serene says if you're still in bed when the last bell rings, you're helping me clean the courtyard.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: She didn't say that.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: No. But she might, once I suggest it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I'm getting up.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Breakfast won't wait forever!

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: There you are. I saved you some bread.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You did?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *grins* Mother Serene wouldn’t let me eat it.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Sit down, Caelan. Before your brother decides you aren’t coming.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Have you been up long?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Long enough to wish there were another pair of hands in the kitchen.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I offered.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: You offered to taste things.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Someone ought to.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *smiles* Very public-spirited of you.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Thank you.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Enjoy a quiet breakfast while you can. Tomorrow we’ll have everyone coming and going for the Festival of Light.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: And today?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Today we make sure everything—and everyone—is ready for it.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: That sounds like rather more work.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: *with a small smile* It usually is.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Your cup’s here, Mother.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Thank you, Caelan. Now, could you both spare me a little time?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: I promised to look in on three households this morning, but there’s more here than I can leave unattended.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Who needs us?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: *with concern* Halden first. This is his medicine. His joints have been troubling him again.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: He’ll tell us they’re perfectly well.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: He probably will. He’s milling flour for the Festival of Light, and I suspect he’s trying to carry every sack himself.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is there much left to do?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Enough to keep the village kitchens waiting if he overworks himself. He should be at his cottage, just south of the mill.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Across the upper bridge?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Yes. Go with Caelan and see whether he needs a hand.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: There’s bread and lamp oil for Elira, too. She’ll be getting her lantern ready for the Festival of Light.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll call on her.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: She should be at home, by the southern bridge. Please ask how she’s doing while you’re there.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Of course.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: And these supplies are for the Venns, up on the eastern terrace. Their little one’s still recovering.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *more quietly* Any better?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: A little, last I heard. They’ve had their hands full between that and the plot.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll see to them.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Thank you. Halden first, then visit the other two in whichever order suits you.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Shall I come for all three?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Come back after Halden. I’ll need your help with the sanctuary preparations.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I was hoping for something interesting.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Then start by helping someone who needs you.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *to Tomas* Come on. You can decide how interesting it was afterward.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Nearly there. This fitting has other ideas.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *grumbles* Serene sent you? I’m not so frail that I need someone counting my aches.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: She sent the medicine you asked about last week.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I said I’d think about asking.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *grins* That’s practically a yes, for you.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Hmph. And which one of you came to do actual work?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: What needs moving?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Those three sacks of flour by the door. Onto the dry pallet. I’ve more coming through the mill and nowhere sensible to put it.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: All this for tomorrow?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: People want their flour before they start baking for the Festival of Light. They’ve been very particular about telling me that.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We’ll make some room.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: One sack at a time. They’re heavier than they look.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I’ll take the middle one.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: You’ll wait until your brother’s ready.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: There. That’s better.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: You can actually get through the doorway now.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I could get through it before.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Carrying one of those?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *after a pause* …I spent forty years carrying these myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Then perhaps you’ve earned the right to let someone else carry a few.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Hmph. Tell Serene I’ll take the medicine.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: She’ll be pleased.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: And if she asks, the wheel’s been making a dreadful racket. I’ll have it looked at.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Ask Mira. If anyone can repair it, she can.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: She’s got her own repairs to finish.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: One more reason to ask before it becomes a bigger job.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: You’ve been listening to Serene.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *with a small smile* Both of us have. It’s difficult not to.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I’d better get back. Mother needs help with the preparations.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Go on. I’ve still got Elira by the southern bridge and the Venns up on the eastern terrace.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: You’ll be back before we’ve finished, then?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: That depends how much you get done.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *rolls his eyes* Oh, very good.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: And try not to turn the courtyard into a workshop.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *grins* No promises.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: *with a wry smile* A delivery from Serene? I swear she thinks I live on bread and stubbornness.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: She mentioned lamp oil, too.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Sensible woman. I was nearly out. Come in, Caelan.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Getting ready for tomorrow?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: *sighs* Trying to. I put the lantern safely out of the way, and now I can’t reach the wretched thing.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Up there?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Yes. The stool’s beneath the shelf. Would you fetch it for me?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Of course.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Gently, mind. I’ve got enough to mend without giving myself another job.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: *looks over the lantern* Thank you. I can clean it here.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You’re carrying this one for your husband again?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: I am. He used to say he only came to the Festival of Light to hear me sing.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Did he?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: *laughs* The old liar couldn’t carry a tune himself. Never stopped him joining in.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Will tomorrow be difficult?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: *her smile softens* Parts of it, perhaps. I still turn to tell him things. Then I remember.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: *after a quiet moment* But remembering him isn’t the same as losing him again. There’s plenty I’m glad to remember.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’m glad you’re coming.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: So am I. And you’ll be there?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I wouldn’t miss it.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Good. Tell Serene I’ll bring the lantern myself. She’s done enough carrying things for me today.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll tell her.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Caelan. Is that from the sanctuary?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Serene asked me to bring these round. How’s the little one?

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: *with relief* Finally keeping food down. We’ve had a quieter morning, thank the gods.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: That’s good to hear.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Please thank Serene for us. I meant to come down myself, but—

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *gently* You’ve had enough to manage.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: If this channel would cooperate, we might get a few things finished.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: What’s happened now?

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: *sighs* The gate’s caught. There’s water in the brook and hardly any reaching the far end of our plot. I can’t keep carrying buckets across all afternoon.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: May I take a look?

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Please. It’s east of the cottage. Look at the pin, then the channel below it.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Borrow what you need from the tool box.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll see what I can do.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The pin’s caught at an angle. I’ll need to take the pressure off before I set it straight.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Twigs have collected below the gate. I’ll need to clear those, too.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I could use their tools. Or perhaps I can push the water back long enough to free the pin.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *quietly* I can’t move it. I’ll need the tools.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: There it goes. That should reach the far end now.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: One less thing to worry about.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Has it been catching often?

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Often enough. They’ve got pumps in the capital that could fill these channels in half the time.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: And payments that would take twice as long to finish.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: *defensively* I know. I’m only saying it would be useful.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: For today, at least, you’ve got the water moving again.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: You’ve done us a kindness. Let Serene know we’ll be all right.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I will. I hope we see you at the festival.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: We’ll see how the little one feels. I’d like that.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: And if we do get there, I intend to sit down for a while.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: *with a small laugh* You say that now.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll leave you to it. Take care.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Caelan, can you look at this?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: What's wrong?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: It turns most of the way, then it sticks. I can't see what's catching.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is the pin bent?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I thought so, but it looks straight.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Have you shown Mira?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Not yet. I wanted to get it working myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You can still ask her.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I know. I will if I can't find it.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: One more adjustment. Then I really am getting back to the preparations.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Should I tell Mother Serene that?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Tell her the preparations are progressing. That covers both things.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: One more adjustment. Then I really am getting back to the preparations.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Should I tell Mother Serene that?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Tell her the preparations are progressing. That covers both things.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: There you are. How is everyone?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Halden finally accepted the medicine. We moved his flour sacks into the dry.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Did he let you help without an argument?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Not entirely.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: *smiles* I’d have worried if he had.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Elira has the bread and oil. She’s bringing her husband’s lantern tomorrow.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Good. I’m glad she wants to come.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: And the Venns have their supplies. The little one’s keeping food down. Their irrigation gate was caught, so I got the channel running again.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: You’ve had a busy morning.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: A useful one, I think.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: You have. And how were they, aside from what needed fixing?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Halden’s doing more than his joints can bear. Elira misses her husband. The Venns are tired—and worried about what next season will cost them.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: I’m glad you stayed long enough to hear that.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You knew I’d find more than deliveries.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: I hoped you’d have time for people. It’s easy to think our work is finished when the baskets are empty.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Then I suppose we keep showing up.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: *warmly* That’s a good place to begin.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Caelan! That dreadful wheel’s finally stopped altogether.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You said it was making a noise.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: And now it isn’t making any noise. That’s worse!

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Did you ask Mira to look at it?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: That’s why I’m here. I could use her help—and another pair of hands, if you can spare him.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll go with her.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: There are kitchens waiting on that flour. I’d rather they didn’t all come asking me about it at once.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Mira should be at her workbench, outside the workshop before the upper bridge.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll stop there on my way to the mill.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *with relief* Thank you.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: And be careful along the channel. Both of you.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: *sets the fitting aside* You have the look of someone bringing me another job.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Could that wait a little?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: That depends. Is someone hurt?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: No. Halden’s mill has stopped.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Ah. I wondered when he’d ask me about that noise.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: He came to the sanctuary himself.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Then it must be serious.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: He needs the flour ready for the Festival of Light. I think he’s already imagining everyone asking where their bread is.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: He’ll have plenty to say if they ask him at once.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: He had plenty to say when it was only me.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: *laughs* Some things keep working.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Will you take a look?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Of course. Let me leave this somewhere I can find it again.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Shall I carry anything?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I’ve got my tools. Come on—we’ll see what the wheel’s doing before he takes anything apart.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *studies the axle* The axle’s still seated. I can’t see anything caught in the wheel.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Neither can I. And nothing’s shifted out of place.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: So we leave it together?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: For now, yes.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Halden will be pleased.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Let’s give him a working mill before we tell him how pleased to be.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *frowns at the trickle* The brook’s moving, but there’s hardly anything coming down this channel.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: There should be a steady flow reaching the wheel.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Just a trickle. That won’t drive it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: No. We’ll need to look further upstream.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: The wheel isn’t getting enough water to turn under load. Something’s restricting the intake.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: A branch, perhaps?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Could be. We’ll know when we see it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We’ll need the upper path.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Back over the upper bridge, then north past the sanctuary steps. Take the road out of the village—the intake’s along that trail.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right. Let’s see what’s caught there.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: We need the north road, past the sanctuary steps. The intake’s along the trail beyond the village.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *points to the limb* There. That limb’s wedged across the screen.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Look how the water’s pressing it into the bars.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We won’t pull it clear like that.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: No. We’ll take the pressure off first.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: And the catch?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Under the water in that little stone recess. We’ll deal with it once the intake’s isolated.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Tell me where you need me.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I’ll set the bypass below the screen. Keep clear while I turn it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Here?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: *checks Caelan is clear* That’s fine. Give me a moment.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The pressure’s easing.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Good. We’ve still got water trapped around the catch, but the main flow’s off it now.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I could move that into the drain.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Just the water in the recess?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes. There’s nowhere for more to come through now.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: All right. I’ll keep clear.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: There. It worked.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: It did. I can reach the catch now.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *a small smile* I thought it would.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: You sound surprised.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Pleased. Mostly.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: And the rest?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *his smile fades a little* I couldn’t do it at the Venns’. I wanted to spare them the trouble, and I still ended up borrowing their tools.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: You were fighting a current there. This was a smaller job.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I know. I just wish I’d managed both.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: You got their water running again, didn’t you?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: *gently* And you’ve cleared this catch for me. Give yourself that much.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right. I’ll try.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I’ll release the catch. Take the rope and keep it steady.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Ready.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Wait until I say. We want the limb clear of the screen.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *nods* I’ve got it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Now. Pull.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: *with relief* There. Hold it a moment… Good. You can let go.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: That’s the water coming through.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: It is. Let’s go back and see what the wheel makes of it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Let’s get back to the wheel and check it’s taking the load. Then we can give Halden some good news.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s plenty of festival flour still to grind.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s plenty of festival flour still to grind.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s plenty of festival flour still to grind.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s plenty of festival flour still to grind.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s plenty of festival flour still to grind.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *smiles* That sounds more like it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: The wheel’s taking the load.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Halden’s dreadful racket.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: He’ll be calling it a lovely sound by now.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Should we let him enjoy it?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: After we tell him what happened. I want him to know which bits he doesn’t need to take apart.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *listens to the wheel* There it is. I was beginning to miss that dreadful racket.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Mira said you would.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: A limb had jammed the intake screen. We freed it and reset the catch.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *raises an eyebrow* We?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Caelan cleared the water from the inspection recess. And did his share of the pulling.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Mira knew what we were looking at.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: And you listened. That helps.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: The wheel itself was sound. You can leave it together.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I hadn’t started.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We thought we’d best hurry.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Hmph. You can both laugh when the flour’s finished.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: How much have you got left?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Enough that I’d rather hear the wheel than the two of you. There are people waiting to start their festival baking.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We’ll leave you to it, then.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Caelan.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *more quietly* My thanks. To both of you.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: You’re welcome.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: There’ll be flour for the Festival of Light. You can tell Serene that.
